6a29da9945bd806eeca0f80b7dedf855203221d1: Garessio 2000 is a small, low-key resort: 12 km of runs for an intimate skiing experience, far from the bustle of the big resorts. This is where people come for calm, authenticity and no queues at the lifts. Garessio 2000's family reputation is well deserved: dedicated beginner areas, well-groomed green runs and a friendly atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It is one of the most reassuring resorts in the Southern Alps for laying the foundations of skiing with children. Garessio 2000's modest altitude, from a base of 1342 m to a summit of 1578 m, makes it sensitive to climate variations. January and February remain the safest months for optimal snow cover. Outside that window, checking the snow reports before you leave is strongly advised. The 28€ day lift pass remains reasonable for the quality of the ski area on offer. Counting accommodation, skiing and meals, Garessio 2000 suits those who want a good week without the final bill knocking them off their chairs. In short, Garessio 2000 does not rival the giants of skiing, and does not claim to. It is an honest destination, often underrated, that deserves to be (re)discovered.

6ab0f16617f57320e2c32655e83ab03b67c4a08b: A resort on a human scale, Campitello di Fassa focuses on the quality of its welcome and its closeness rather than on impressive figures. Its 55 km of runs are a good fit for a stay of 3 to 4 days, especially for families or skiers who don't need to constantly renew their playground. Campitello di Fassa has managed to keep the identity of an authentic mountain village, far from the concrete resorts of the 1970s. People come here for the clean air, the unspoilt landscapes and a friendly atmosphere that stands apart from the industrialisation of skiing in some large ski areas. Campitello di Fassa's altitude (1448 m at the base, 2485 m at the top) helps it maintain decent snow cover in the middle of winter. January and February are the most reliable months; in December and March, it's worth checking conditions before finalising a booking. The budget for a stay in Campitello di Fassa is clearly high: €76 for a day lift pass, plus accommodation and mountain restaurants that are among the most expensive in the Alps. It's the price of excellence — but you should be aware of it before you go. In short: Campitello di Fassa lives up to its promises. A Northern Alps resort that will suit most profiles without disappointing.
